Car wash rule: the moment you go through, it rains. If it's spring, it hails. If it's construction season, gravel dust.
The car wash is sound check for your car. Loud, wet, a little scary, and it comes out ready for the show.
Things nobody says at the car wash: 'I love when the giant spinning brushes slap the windows.'
An automatic car wash is the closest a car gets to a rock concert: lights, foam, spinning things and one nervous moose inside.
Drive-thru order: 'One burger, no pickles.' Speaker: 'kshhh pickles kshhh?' Me: 'No.' Bag: four pickles, no burger.
Ordering at a drive-thru is like sound check. Say it once, they say 'pardon?', say it louder, and somehow you end up with a milkshake.
Drive-thru panic: the moment you pull up to the speaker and forget every food that has ever existed.
Things nobody says at the drive-thru: 'Take your time, the line behind me is very patient.'
The drive-thru speaker sounds like a walkie-talkie at the bottom of a lake. Respect it as gear. Do not trust it with your order.
Why did the car get good grades? It always went the extra kilometre.
Why did the tire go back to school? It wanted to retread the material.
The seat lever: a mystery bar under the seat that either moves you one perfect notch or launches you into the back row.
Adjusting a car seat is like setting up a mic stand. Up, down, forward, back, and somehow you end up right where you started.
Every family has a car called Old Blue, The Beast or 'Mom's car.' My truck is named Gord. Gord is a beauty.
My truck Gord has 400,000 kilometres on him. He doesn't go fast. He goes forever. Beauty.
Every car has one dashboard light nobody understands. Ours looks like a teapot doing a cartwheel. The manual just says 'see dealer.'
Nobody names the rental car. You just call it 'the rental,' like it's on a temporary contract. Which it is.
Why do minivans have sliding doors? So you can slide out of the argument about who ate the last chip.
The minivan is the most underrated vehicle in rock history. We fit a whole band and a drum kit in one in '97. The drum kit got the best seat.
My truck Gord still has a tape deck. I own one tape. It's Loud Prairie's first album. It's not good. I love it.
Heated seats: Canada's greatest invention after ketchup chips and gaffer tape. Beauty.
Remote starters exist so your car can warm up while you warm up to the idea of leaving the house.
My truck's horn sounds like a sad duck. I've used it once. A duck answered.
Leather car seats in July get as hot as a stage light. Twenty years of tours and nothing prepared me for that first sit.
The windshield sunshade is the hardest piece of origami you will ever fail to fold.
Spare tire: the backup singer of the car world. Nobody notices until they're needed, then they save the whole show. Beauty.
Air freshener scents I'd buy: 'Fresh Sound Check,' 'Tour Bus at 2 a.m.' and 'Mystery Fry.' Okay, maybe not that last one.
New car smell is just a smell that hasn't met a road trip yet.
Every pickup in Alberta has a toolbox in the back with one wrench and four work gloves that don't match.
The dashboard isn't a shelf. Tell that to the receipts, sunglasses and three-month-old parking stub living up there.
The car manual: the only book in the house nobody has read, yet everybody says 'check the manual.'
Gord's bumper sticker says 'I brake for gophers.' It's not a joke. It's a lifestyle.
Mechanic: Your alternator's done. Me: Can we tape it? Mechanic: No, Doug. Me: Gaffer tape, though? Mechanic: Still no.
Windshield wipers have two speeds: 'barely moving' and 'Kev at the encore.'
A squeaky windshield wiper is a song with one note that never ends. Rodney wrote a song like that once.
Gord's radio gets two stations: classic rock and the farm report. I know more about canola prices than any roadie alive.
Some people modify their engines. I modified my sunroof so the antlers fit. Gord's sort of a convertible now.
Car show guy: What's under the hood? Me: Twenty years of granola bar wrappers and one guitar pick. Gord's a classic.
Car wash vacuum: four minutes of power, three of them spent trying to reach the one fry under the seat.
The car wash deluxe option is the same wash with coloured foam. I paid extra for the light show. Worth it. Beauty.
Drive-thru menus change faster than a group chat name. Every time I pull up, there's a new sandwich and my old favourite is gone.
Drive-thru: 'Anything else?' Me: 'No.' 'Anything else?' Me: 'Uh, a pie?' I have never once ordered a pie on purpose.
Key fob batteries always run out when you're carrying three bags. Like sound check: the problem waits until your hooves are full.
Why was the car so popular at band practice? Great horn section.
Finding your car in a big parking lot by pressing the lock button and listening for the beep is basically echolocation. Moose are great at it.
Things nobody says: 'I remember exactly where I parked.'
Seat warmer on high for twenty minutes: you're not warm anymore. You're toast.
Alberta's four seasons: winter, still winter, construction and the one perfect afternoon in September.
A chinook is Alberta weather doing a key change in the middle of the song.
Chinook day: minus twenty at breakfast, plus ten by lunch. Wear layers like a sound tech. You'll peel off half of them by noon.
Chinooks make every jacket the wrong jacket. Every time. No exceptions.
Mosquitoes in Alberta are so big, they show up at the tour bus with their own backstage passes.
Fun fact: Alberta mosquitoes can hear a screen door open from three kilometres away. Science says no. My arms say yes.
Mosquito season is a summer festival where you're the snack table.
Mosquito math: one bite is bad luck. Two is a pattern. Three means it's June in Alberta.
Bug spray is the summer rider. Non-negotiable. Right on the list under 'snacks.'
Mosquito bites are the worst tour souvenir. You don't even get a T-shirt.
Hailstones the size of peas, then golf balls, then peas again. Alberta weather can't commit to a ball size.
Construction season: when the orange cones come out of hibernation and spread across the province like gophers.
Orange traffic cones are the official flower of Alberta in July.
Construction season is Alberta's longest-running festival. Headliner: orange cones. Opening act: more orange cones.
Alberta construction season: the only jam session where nobody brings an instrument.
Road construction sign: 'Expect delays.' Me: I toured with Rodney for twenty years. I always expect delays.
Spring potholes are so deep, I lost a drumstick in one. Kev's still waiting for it to come back.
Alberta potholes: where your car learns to play the drums.
A pothole and a slushie in the cupholder: a quick lesson in why lids were invented.
Magpies are the roadies of the bird world: loud, clever and they'll take anything shiny you leave lying around.
Magpies sound like a group chat: everybody talking, nobody listening, somebody upset about a french fry.
Gophers in a field are like a concert crowd. One pops up, then another, then they all just stand there staring at you.
Gophers are Alberta's front row. Always up, always watching, never once bought a ticket.
Why did the gopher make a great roadie? Always pops up right when you need a hand. Tiny hand, but still.
First snowfall is Alberta doing a sound check for winter.
Fun fact: Alberta's first snow arrives exactly one day after you pack away your winter coat. Not science. Just tradition.
First snow in Alberta: everybody acts shocked. It happens every year. Sometimes in September. Once, in my memory, in June.
Things nobody says in Alberta: 'Thank goodness, the mosquitoes are back.' 'I hope construction lasts longer.' 'What a lovely pothole.'
Spring in Alberta lasts about two days between the last snow and the first mosquito. Blink and you'll be swatting.
Prairie thunderstorms are the loudest show I've ever heard, and I worked twenty years for a rock band.
Alberta summer: daylight until almost eleven at night. Great for road trips. Terrible for convincing anyone it's bedtime.
Outdoor show forecast: dry for weeks. Day of the show: a month of rain in one afternoon. Every time.
Fall in Alberta: leaves turn gold, the air gets crisp and somewhere a moose starts shopping for a toque with antler holes.
Alberta weather forecast: sunny, cloudy, hail, snow, chinook. That's not a forecast. That's a setlist.
Magpies versus gophers: Alberta's longest-running rivalry, and nobody's keeping score.
Washed my truck Gord on Tuesday. By Wednesday, the magpies had reviewed it.
Every Alberta garage keeps a snow shovel, a lawn mower and a rake within reach, because May might need all three.
Alberta in May: shovel snow at breakfast, sunburn by lunch. Pack a toque and sunscreen in the same bag.
Chinook headaches, chinook jackets, chinook arches. Calgary has a whole merch line for one wind.
The wind in southern Alberta doesn't blow. It rearranges.
Gophers don't study. They just pop up and guess. Honestly, respect.
Mosquitoes in Alberta don't bite. They take samples.
Mosquito repellent smells like a lemon that's angry about something.
The difference between a pothole and a crater: about two weeks in April.
After hail season, car lots start calling dimpled cars 'a deal.' Alberta: where even the weather does bodywork.
A magpie once watched me eat a granola bar for twenty minutes. Didn't ask. Didn't blink. Just negotiated with its eyes.
Gopher fun fact: they hold a meeting every morning to decide who pops up first. I made that up. Probably true.
Potholes have life stages: baby potholes in March, teenage potholes in April, full-grown legends by May.
The first warm day of spring in Alberta: everybody's in shorts, and the snowbank is still taller than the fence.
A chinook once melted all the snow off Brenda's roof in an hour. Next morning, she was an ice rink. Alberta, pick a lane.
August in Alberta: one yellow leaf shows up and everybody starts whispering about snow.
Lowkey the best part of any road trip is the gas station. The destination is just the excuse.
A gas station sandwich at noon is mid. The same sandwich at 2 a.m. after a load-out is a five-star meal.
Bro thought he could carry every grocery bag from the car in one trip. I have four legs and I still make two trips.
The ick: when the aux cord crackles every time somebody shifts in their seat. Get a new cord, Kev.
Main character moment: the car wash foam turns pink just as your favourite song comes on.
Caught in 4K: the drive-thru camera filming me say 'pardon?' for the fourth time.
No cap, magpies are the smartest birds in Alberta. They know your car, your face and your lunch schedule.
Mosquitoes in June are delulu. They genuinely think they were invited.
A chinook is giving spring for exactly one afternoon.
The ick: finding a week-old fry under the car seat and it's still somehow soft.
Minivans are lowkey the coolest vehicle out there. Sliding doors, endless cupholders and room for a full amp stack.
Main character energy: the one gopher standing alone in an empty field like it's got a spotlight.
Bro thought 'five more minutes' on the alarm meant five more minutes.
No cap, the best seat in any car is the one closest to the snacks.
Lowkey the best study snack is the one in the cupboard you were told to save for later.
Being the DJ on a road trip is main character pressure. One bad song and you're back to holding the snacks.
Rodney once said 'I don't need the GPS.' Caught in 4K forty minutes later, asking a gopher for directions.
It's giving festival: mud on your boots, a sunburn on one arm and somebody else's glow stick in your pocket.
Group chat delulu: 'Let's all study together at 8 a.m. Saturday.' Nobody in that chat has ever been awake at 8 a.m. on a Saturday.
Lowkey, a perfectly coiled cable is the most satisfying thing on Earth. Over, under, over, under. Beauty.
The ick: wet socks after a festival. The cure: dry socks. Tour secret. Always pack two pairs.
NPC energy: the GPS saying 'continue straight' for three hours across Saskatchewan.
